'''Nijaz Ibrulj''' (born 2 July 1956) is a [[Bosnians|Bosnian]] [[philosopher]] and a professor at the [[University of Sarajevo]]'s Department of Philosophy and Sociology. He lectures on [[logic]], [[analytic philosophy]], methodology of social sciences, theory of knowledge, and [[cognitive science]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.ff.unsa.ba/index.php?option=com_contact&catid=14&Itemid=52|title=Filozofski fakultet Univerziteta u Sarajevu|access-date=2010-03-23|archive-date=2010-02-09|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100209034352/http://www.ff.unsa.ba/index.php?option=com_contact&catid=14&Itemid=52|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>Ibrulj, Nijaz ''Bosnia Porphyriana. An Outline of the Development of Logic in Bosnia and Herzegovina'' in ''Pregled'', 2, 2009.</ref> His interests also extend to the field of social ontology. Ibrulj was awarded a [[Fulbright Program|Fulbright Visiting Scholarship]] during the 2000-2001 academic years to visit the [[University of California, Berkeley]]. His application was sponsored by [[John Searle]] and [[Donald Davidson (philosopher)|Donald Davidson]].<ref>http://www.zrs-kp.si/EN/zaposleni/bibliografija_in_projekti.htm {{Dead link|date=February 2022}}</ref>

==Academic activities==
Ibrulj is the founder and president of  the [[Academia Analitica]], a [[scientific society]] for the development of logic and analytic philosophy in Bosnia and Herzegovina and leader of the "ZINK", a scientific and research incubator.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Članovi Udruženja Academia Analitica |url=http://www.academia-analitica.org/index.php?option=com_content&view=section&layout=blog&id=3&Itemid=9 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120429190856/http://www.academia-analitica.org/index.php?option=com_content&view=section&layout=blog&id=3&Itemid=9 |archive-date=2012-04-29 |access-date=2025-07-07 |website=www.academia-analitica.org |language=hr-hr |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://ziink.wordpress.com/clanovi-2/mentori/|title=Mentori|date=28 March 2008|access-date=20 March 2010|archive-date=13 May 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100513060036/http://ziink.wordpress.com/clanovi-2/mentori/|url-status=live}}</ref> He is the founding editor of ''SOPHOS'', a young researchers’ journal and of ''The Logical Foresight'', a journal for logic and science.

==Work in philosophy==
Ibrulj has written extensively on various topics of analytic philosophy, [[philosophical logic]], and philosophy of language, cognitive science and social ontology.

In his book ''Philosophy of Logic (1999)'', he introduced a theory named the Principle of the Logical. He defines the Principle of the Logical as an ideal matrix of  the logical principles or [[laws of thought]] (the [[law of identity]], the [[law of non-contradiction]], the [[law of excluded middle]], the law of sufficient reason).<ref>Ibrulj ''Philosophy of Logic'' (1999), ch. 4, pp. 187-226</ref>

In the book ''The Century of Rearrangement'' (2005), Ibrulj investigated the concepts of relation between identity and knowledge in an ambient of intelligent space, which is designed by modern informational and communicational technology, nanoscience and [[nanotechnology]], and the processes of [[globalization|globalisation]]. He made a distinction between two theories of identity: a strong theory of identity (“anchored identity”) and a weak theory of identity (“mobile identity” or “identity in action”).<ref>Ibrulj ''The Century of Rearrangements. Essays on Identity, Knowledge and Society.'' (2005), pp. 17-49</ref><ref>{{cite book| last = Arnautović| first = Samir| title = Transcendentalna filozofija i odrednice moderne| year = 2009| publisher = Filozofsko društvo "Theoria"| isbn = 978-9958-9419-2-4 }}</ref>

Ibrulj has also translated from [[English language|English]] (Donald Davidson), [[German language|German]] (Gottlob Frege), and [[Ancient Greek]] (Bosnian–Greek edition of [[Porphyry (geology)|Porphyry]]'s [[Isagoge]]).<ref>Premec, Vladimir ''Kulturnoznanstvena vrednota'' in ''Dijalog'', 1, 2009.</ref>
